input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay, triggered by a minor breach (late payment of any invoice) and uncapped, so it can quickly exceed the remaining contract value — walk-away territory under the rule, well short of both the preferred (no Customer-payable LDs) and fallback (single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees) positions. Termination in Section 9.4 carries no early-termination fee, so no capped LD amount is needed elsewhere; service credits in favour of us are unaffected. We propose replacing the LD with ordinary late-payment interest on undisputed amounts.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with simple late-payment interest.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, particularly at 15% of annual Fees per week, which is uncapped and disproportionate to a late invoice. We have replaced it with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with Section 7.3.

ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar charge in respect of late payment.
